payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The battery demonstrated gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. Its principal operational limitation is a 4 °C temperature floor, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte and cycling must stop.

FLAGS: Source A and the unpublished pre-audit draft report “12,000 cycles,” whereas finalized Source C establishes “8,400 cycles” as the governing figure; the summary correctly reflects the correction.
VERDICT: APPROVE
